# Text Adventure Engine

Zork-era adventures are secretly the perfect functional-programming demo:

- The **world is a value** — a nested map of rooms, exits, items and flags.
- A **turn is a pure function**: `(step world command) → [world' text]`. No globals, no mutation, no I/O inside the engine.
- A **playthrough is a reduce** over the command list.

Because the engine is pure, saving is trivial (keep the value), undo is trivial (keep the old value), and testing is trivial (assert on the returned world). The Clojure cell (ClojureScript, running in your browser) runs a scripted playthrough and publishes the transcript; JS renders it like a terminal.

(require '[clojure.string :as str])

;; ---- The world is data. Edit it like data. -------------------------
(def world
  {:here :cell
   :inventory #{}
   :flags #{}
   :rooms
   {:cell    {:desc "A damp stone cell. A rusty COT sits in the corner."
              :exits {:north :corridor}
              :items #{:key}
              :hidden {:key "Under the cot you find a small brass KEY."}}
    :corridor {:desc "A torch-lit corridor. A heavy DOOR blocks the way north."
               :exits {:south :cell :north :vault}
               :locked #{:north}}
    :vault   {:desc "The vault! Gold everywhere. A LADDER leads up to daylight."
              :exits {:up :outside}
              :items #{:gold}}
    :outside {:desc "Fresh air. Freedom. The morning sun on your face."}}})

;; ---- One pure function. (step world cmd) -> [world' text] ----------
(defn step [w [verb noun]]
  (let [room ((:rooms w) (:here w))]
    (case verb
      :look [w (:desc room)]

      :search
      (if-let [msg (get (:hidden room) noun)]
        [(-> w
             (update-in [:rooms (:here w) :items] conj noun)
             (update-in [:rooms (:here w) :hidden] dissoc noun))
         msg]
        [w "You find nothing special."])

      :take
      (if (contains? (:items room) noun)
        [(-> w
             (update :inventory conj noun)
             (update-in [:rooms (:here w) :items] disj noun))
         (str "Taken: " (name noun) ".")]
        [w "No such thing here."])

      :unlock
      (if (and (contains? (:inventory w) :key)
               (contains? (:locked room) noun))
        [(update-in w [:rooms (:here w) :locked] disj noun)
         "The key turns with a satisfying clunk."]
        [w "It won't budge."])

      :go
      (let [dest (get (:exits room) noun)]
        (cond
          (nil? dest) [w "You can't go that way."]
          (contains? (:locked room) noun) [w "Locked."]
          :else [(assoc w :here dest)
                 (get-in w [:rooms dest :desc])]))

      [w "The dungeon does not understand."])))

;; ---- A playthrough is a reduce over commands. -----------------------
(def script
  [[:look nil] [:go :north] [:go :north] [:go :south] [:search :key]
   [:take :key] [:go :north] [:unlock :north] [:go :north]
   [:take :gold] [:go :up]])

(def result
  (reduce (fn [{:keys [w log]} cmd]
            (let [[w2 text] (step w cmd)]
              {:w w2
               :log (conj log {:cmd (str/join " " (map #(if % (name %) "") cmd))
                               :text text})}))
          {:w world :log []}
          script))

(doseq [{:keys [cmd text]} (:log result)]
  (println (str "> " cmd))
  (println (str "  " text)))

(let [w (:w result)]
  (println)
  (println "escaped:" (= :outside (:here w))
           "| carrying gold:" (contains? (:inventory w) :gold))
  ;; the ORIGINAL world value is untouched - purity means free save-states
  (println "original world still starts in:" (name (:here world))))

;; room texts deliberately contain no double quotes, so plain
;; concatenation emits valid JSON
(println (str "__NB_SET__ {\"key\":\"adventure\",\"value\":{\"turns\":["
              (str/join ","
                (map (fn [{:keys [cmd text]}]
                       (str "{\"cmd\":\"" cmd "\",\"text\":\"" text "\"}"))
                     (:log result)))
              "],\"escaped\":" (= :outside (:here (:w result)))
              ",\"gold\":" (contains? (:inventory (:w result)) :gold) "}}"))

## Why FP fits this genre

Look at what the engine *never* does: no room object mutates, no global inventory, no event listeners. Each turn produces a **new world value**, and the old ones are still there — which is why "the original world still starts in: cell" prints at the end. Save-scumming, replays, undo, and "what if I'd taken the other exit?" are all the same operation: keep a reference.

The `case` on verbs is the whole parser; adding a verb never risks breaking another — there's no shared state to trample.

## Try this

- Add a `:drop` verb (inverse of `:take`) — it's four lines, and the type of `step` doesn't change.
- Add a troll to the corridor that blocks `:north` until you `[:give :gold]` — a flag in `:flags`, a guard in `:go`. Then re-order the script so you *can't* win, and watch the transcript tell the story.
- Write `(defn undo [history] ...)` — with this engine it's `pop`.
- Branch the timeline: reduce the same world over **two** different scripts and diff the final inventories. Two parallel universes, zero copies.
